newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti says will discuss mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti says will discuss mini-budget.

text.p: The leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party said on Wednesday he was ready to discuss the government's planned mini-budget but would not accept cuts in public spending or new taxes.

"We will not run away from any discussion," Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said in a statement after Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he would be launching a mini-budget in the coming weeks to enable Italy to meet the single currency criteria in full.
"As ever, the decisive word is contents...Communist Refoundation will not accept cuts in public spending or new taxes," he said.
Prodi depends on support from Communist Refoundation for a majority in parliament.

Bertinotti said he was "not convinced" of the need for a mini-budget and said he was concerned for the unemplopyed and pensioners. Prodi's has not said how big the planned mini-budget will be, but has said it will be based on structural measures.
